relations: Olive resting on the frosted ice face permits slow rolling and seam drift toward the top.
A single transitional frame shatters the sphere into scattered green and pale fragments around the ice.
Those fragments settle into a flattened teardrop mass wedged at the ice base against horizontal corks.
The ice shard, corks, and warm backdrop persist unchanged while the olive deforms.
caption: The video captures a macro still-life set against a warm orange-tan gradient, where several wine corks form a base and an upright cork at the left bears a cursive "Barossa" label. A translucent, frosted ice shard is balanced across the horizontal corks, and a whole green olive rests on the upper-right face of that ice. Through the first stretch the ice and corks stay put while the olive slowly rolls and rotates on the frosted face, its surface seam drifting from the left edge toward the top. A sudden disruption then appears in a single transitional frame, where the olive breaks into scattered green and pale fragments around the ice face. In the following frames the olive is no longer a sphere on top but a flattened, teardrop-shaped green mass settled low at the base of the ice. This deformed mass wedges against the horizontal corks while the ice behind it shows its bare frosted crown. The mass stays motionless for the rest of the excerpt, the corks and warm backdrop unchanged.
